verification_report.summary: All items in section_smooth_dual_sharpness_v2.tex pass in source order. Smooth dual attainment makes the density smooth before the L^p cluster theorem is used; normalized clusters are uniquely identified by threshold-subsolution rigidity. In the Kähler case the first-order equation propagates one positive value of the smooth coefficient along paths, proving strict positivity. The nonclosed example is globally Hermitian by its two-region estimate, has a nonzero smooth density vanishing on an open set, satisfies b_omega(f)=1 by the explicit subsolution and the same normalized Gauduchon test, and uses only ddc(gamma^(n-1))=0 for Stokes. Its normalized current is a smooth strictly positive maximizer, and closedness is ruled out noncircularly by the preceding characterization. The dimension-one comparison and the final normalized convergence statement are also valid. No bounded-mass, positive-lower-mass, or closed-Gauduchon-metric assumption is used.
